purpose: Back up COPIES of the live ai-memory data dir and a Qdrant snapshot (taken through the Qdrant API into a scratch dir, without modifying live collections) with restic, restore into scratch, rebind a disposable ai-memory instance on another port and a disposable Qdrant instance (pinned binary, scratch storage, other ports) against the restored data, and verify reads (page count, a known query for ai-memory; collection point count and one search for Qdrant), then clean up scratch processes.
preregistered: If the restic-restored ai-memory data dir starts cleanly under a disposable `ai-memory serve --data-dir <restored> --bind 127.0.0.1:<new-port>` process (no crash, no unresolved migration error) and the restored dir's page/session/observation counts and a fixed FTS query ('handoff', workspace=agent-lab, project=agent-lab) return the same top-ranked page paths as a pre-backup baseline read of the copy, that narrows open_gaps[4] (local, non-hosted-runner rebinding evidence for ai-memory) toward closed. If a disposable Qdrant process loaded from the restic-restored API snapshot reports the same points_count as the live collection at snapshot time, and a deterministic payload-filter search (collectionName=codegraph_7c79759d30d0) returns the same point id as observed on the live collection, that narrows open_gaps[4] for Qdrant and cross-checks open_gaps[2] (independent-domain restore) using a local restic-mediated round trip rather than the prior GitHub-hosted-runner-only evidence. A crash, a migration error, a missing/renamed page, a search result that disagrees with the baseline, a point-count mismatch, or a search miss would each refute the corresponding narrowing claim and must be recorded as such rather than retried.

result: CORRECTED 2026-09-23: the ai-memory reads below went to the live server, not the copies; the coordinator_rerun block replaces them with isolated reads, which pass. Original text follows. ai-memory: a read-only copy of the live 371 MiB data dir was restic-backed-up and restored byte-for-byte (restic check --read-data reported no errors). A disposable `ai-memory serve` instance bound to 127.0.0.1:49399 started cleanly against the restored copy with no migration errors (schema already at the binary's current version 64) and served MCP over HTTP. Reads against the restored data (CLI status/search, which access the SQLite store directly) reproduced the pre-backup baseline exactly for pages_latest (117), pages_all (393) and sessions (175), and the fixed 'handoff' query returned byte-identical top-3 ranked results (same paths, titles, snippets and FTS5 rank scores) before and after the round trip; the observations count grew slightly post-restore (139312 -> 139377) which is attributable to the disposable instance's own startup/scheduled-maintenance activity after rebind, not to data loss. Qdrant: a snapshot of the live 'socraticode_metadata' collection (4 points) was created through the Qdrant HTTP API (a read-only operation against the collection) and downloaded to scratch with a matching sha256 checksum. A disposable Qdrant 1.19.1 process, started with scratch storage/snapshot paths and HTTP port 26333 (no gRPC), recovered the restic-restored snapshot into a new collection 'socraticode_metadata_restored' reporting points_count 4 (equal to the live count at snapshot time) and status 'green'. A deterministic payload-filter search (collectionName=codegraph_7c79759d30d0) returned exactly the same point id (REDACTED-POINT-ID-1) with its full payload intact as observed on the live collection before the snapshot. Both disposable processes were terminated with SIGTERM and confirmed absent from the process list; the live ai-memory service and the live Qdrant collection list were unaffected throughout (live qdrant-agent-lab.service still shows exactly its original 9 collections with no new/renamed entries), and the snapshot file created on the live Qdrant server was deleted afterward as cleanup.

verdict_impact.explanation: Produces the first local, non-hosted-runner evidence that both pinned applications (ai-memory, Qdrant) can be restic-backed-up, restored and rebound to a disposable instance with reads verified byte-identical to a pre-backup baseline, narrowing open_gaps[4] (rebinding after restore) and cross-checking open_gaps[2] (independent-domain restore, previously only demonstrated on one GitHub-hosted runner) with a same-host but locally-executed round trip. It supports the incumbent restic+pinned-binary approach rather than refuting it. It does not close open_gaps[2] fully: this is still the same physical host (not a genuinely independent machine), snapshots were taken sequentially rather than atomically across the two applications (per the layer's own open_gaps[4] text on non-atomicity), and reboot/power-loss recovery was not exercised.

limitations: Same-host execution: this is a new scratch data dir and disposable ports on the same WSL machine that runs the live services, not a second physical or virtual host, so it does not close the 'independent physical host' sub-claim of open_gaps[2].

The Qdrant collection used (socraticode_metadata, 4 points) is SocratiCode's own metadata store, not an ai-memory-owned Qdrant collection -- ai-memory on this host stores its embeddings in SQLite, not Qdrant, so 'a Qdrant snapshot' in this check exercises the same pinned Qdrant binary and restic path that an ai-memory-adjacent Qdrant deployment would use, but is not literally ai-memory's own vector store. This is recorded as a substitution, not concealed.

Snapshots/copies of the two applications were taken sequentially (ai-memory copy first, then the Qdrant snapshot moments later), not atomically as a single point-in-time cut across both applications; open_gaps[4]'s own text already flags this as a residual, unresolved by this check.

The observations-count drift (139312 -> 139377) after rebind was attributed to the disposable instance's own startup/maintenance writes rather than independently proven line-by-line; this is a reasonable but not exhaustively verified explanation.
Only one collection and one ai-memory workspace/project scope were exercised; broader multi-collection or multi-tenant restore behavior is untested.
restic repository password was a fixed test string ('gap-resolution-20260922-test'), acceptable for a disposable scratch repo but not representative of production secret handling.
No reboot or power-loss fault injection was performed (out of scope for this check, tracked separately under open_gaps[2]'s remaining needs_hardware items).

Absolute paths recorded above have the host username normalized to this repo's publication-hygiene placeholder (scripts/validate.py PRIVATE_CONTENT rules). ai-memory session-path and Qdrant point identifiers were redacted to REDACTED-*-ID placeholders (raw UUID-format identifiers are flagged by the same rule); the unredacted values were compared byte-for-byte during execution and are retained only in the scratch artifacts referenced under raw_artifacts, outside this repo.

The first run's ai-memory status/search evidence is void (it read the live store); only coordinator_rerun establishes the ai-memory read comparison. The disposable servers' own start-up is from the first run.

coordinator_rerun.reason: Finding from the Codex blind review of PR #81 (gpt-6-astra, read-only, 2026-09-22), confirmed by the retained raw files: the first run's `ai-memory status` and `ai-memory search` calls passed only --data-dir, and the CLI sends those calls to the server at its default server_url (the live server, 127.0.0.1:49374). baseline-status.json reports data_dir ~/.local/share/ai-memory and restored-status.json logs server_url=http://127.0.0.1:49374, so both 'reads' queried the live store. They compared the live store with itself and established nothing about the restore.
coordinator_rerun.method: Restore the same restic snapshot again into a new target; diff it against the pre-backup copy; start two disposable servers (a copy of the pre-backup copy on 127.0.0.1:49411, the fresh restore on 127.0.0.1:49412); send every client read to its own server with AI_MEMORY_SERVER_URL; accept a read only when the status output's data_dir and bind name that arm's directory and port.

coordinator_rerun.result: The fresh restore is byte-identical to the pre-backup copy (diff -r: no output, exit 0). Each disposable server answered for its own directory. Counts are equal (pages_latest 117, pages_all 393, sessions 175, observations 139312), and the top three 'handoff' results are the same pages in the same order. The first run's 'observations slightly higher' was the live store growing, not server bookkeeping.
